full_judgment: 2. Facts as placed before the High Court Division, in short, are that petitioner No. 1 who started his career on 20-3-1968 as a Lecturer of Chemistry in the Carmichael College and on 16-12-2003 retired as Principal of the Palashbari Government College at Gaibandha after a teaching career of thirty-five years. Petitioner No. 2 is his wife and a housewife. On a joint application of the petitioners and two others (wife's full sister and her husband, added respondent No.9), respondent No. 7, Assistant Commissioner issued a letter of allotment dated 14-3-1979 allotting 376 square yards of plot No. 203, Road No. 11 in Block B of Section 12 of Mirpur Housing Estate. Petitioners and other two allotees deposited entire lease money of Taka 50,760 on different dates by treasury 'challan'. Said respondent No. 7, by his letter dated 26-6-1981 modified the order of allotment in respect of quantum of said plot from 376 to 375 square yards and the amount of 'Salami' from Taka 50,625 to Taka 50,625 if paid in installments. Meanwhile, a Sub-Divisional Engineer of the Housing Estate delivered joint possession of aforesaid plot to said allottees vide letter of possession dated 21-3-1981-and on the same date, the petitioners and other two allottees got possession of said plot. After receipt of the entire lease money, said respondent No. 7 on behalf of the President of the Republic executed and registered a lease deed dated 22-2-1982 leasing out said land to the four allottees for 99 years. All four allottees also signed the deed as second party. Then on joint prayer of the said four allottees, the Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha (RAJUK) accorded an approval to the joint plan and design submitted for construction of a building vide memo dated 15-3-1986. On their joint application said respondent No. 7 vide his letter dated 5-5-1988 also permitted said allottees to mortgage the land to the House Building Finance Corporation for loan. They also got the land mutated in their joint names through Mutation Case No. 4893 of 2002 dated 13-5-2002 and possessed the land by payment of rents and taxes to the respective authorities. Their names were also recorded in the Mahanagar Survey and a new khatian was accordingly, prepared in their names. On 8-9-2004, the petitioner received the impugned letter and also news clipping of two national dailies, namely, 'Daily Manabzamin' dated 31-8-2001 and 'Daily Matribhomi', which carried a legal notice issued under the signature of respondent No.4, Deputy Director canceling the lease in respect of the petitioners only under Clause 23(1) of the lease deed. Hence they filed the writ petition challenging the impugned cancellation and obtained the Rule.
